name: Lodore Canyon of the Green River
reach: Gates of Lodore to Split Mountain
agency: Dinosaur National Monument, River Permit Office

camps.name: Pot Creek
camps.desc: Two campsites. The creek runs to the river in spring runoff, and the cliff walls opposite are a playground for desert bighorn sheep.

camps.name: Triplet Falls Beach
camps.desc: A campsite marked by a post just before you hear the rapid.

camps.name: Wild Mountain Beach
camps.desc: There have been sightings of a moose in this area.

camps.name: Limestone Beach
camps.desc: Many shady trees. Hike up the cliffs to the Hanging Garden.

camps.name: Jones Hole
camps.desc: Three sites near the mouth of cold, clear Jones Creek.

camps.name: Compromise Beach
camps.desc: Listed in log order between Jones Hole and Sage Creek; mile is estimated.

camps.name: Cove Beach
camps.desc: Listed in log order below Red Wash Canyon; mile is estimated.

camps.name: Island Park
camps.desc: One site in the flatwater of Island Park.

rapids.name: Winnie's Rapid
rapids.desc: The first rapid. A huge boulder splits the river in half, and the easiest scout is on the right. Avoid the big center boulder and the shallow rocks on river right. A scout trail runs along river left. A pillow rock called Lucifer sits below the first drop; guides suggest riding it.

rapids.name: Buster Basin Creek rapid
rapids.desc: Debris flows from Buster Basin Creek in recent years have made an exciting rapid here.

rapids.name: Upper Disaster Falls
rapids.desc: The first Class IV of the trip. A long, tumultuous rapid with many obstacles that gets harder at certain water levels. Powell's party lost a supply boat here.

rapids.name: Middle Disaster
rapids.desc: Technical. Stay left and read the water. The right side can be dangerous; one group flipped three oar rigs there.

rapids.name: Lower Disaster Falls
rapids.desc: A rock garden with a possibly submerged cobble island right of mid-channel.

rapids.name: Harp Falls
rapids.desc: Marked Class III on the map before Triplet Falls. A 2007 trip noticed no rapid there at low flow.

rapids.name: Triplet Falls
rapids.desc: Three drops through two large turns. Scout river left and run center, right, left. Avoid the rock on river right at the last drop; the run-out can be shallow. Rated III in some sources and IV in others. Poison oak grows near the scouting trail on river left.

rapids.name: Hell's Half Mile
rapids.desc: One of the nation's top-ten "Big Drops". Weave through boulders to the center slot into a wave train, then a quarter mile of rocks, waves and holes that ease gradually. Rated III by American Whitewater and IV in a guidebook. The rapid splits into three channels at the bottom, with a large beach on river left. Lucifer’s Rock sits midway down and can be passed on either side.

rapids.name: Greasy Pliers Rapid
rapids.desc: In Whirlpool Canyon. Not rated individually.

rapids.name: Moonshine Rapid
rapids.desc: In Split Mountain Gorge. Pretty easy: center, then right. Scout left to avoid odd rocks in the last drop. Life jackets required.

rapids.name: S.O.B. Rapid
rapids.desc: In Split Mountain Gorge. Technical. Pass the small center boulder, pull right, then move into the right channel. Scout left.

rapids.name: Inglesby Rapid
rapids.desc: The last rapid in Split Mountain Gorge, just above the take-out.

hikes.name: Winnie's Rapid scout trail
hikes.desc: A trail on river left that overlooks the first drop. Winnie's Grotto and a sandy beach make a good stop.

hikes.name: Hanging Garden
hikes.desc: Hike up the cliffs from Limestone Beach to the Hanging Garden and an overlook.

hikes.name: Echo Park trails
hikes.desc: Pool Creek, petroglyphs on the cliffs, inscriptions by the hermit Pat Lynch, and Whispering Cave, a deep cave that travels far into the mountain. More intricate petroglyphs lie farther along.

hikes.name: Jones Hole
hikes.desc: Hike along the creek, or go 2.5 miles to Ely Creek and Butt Plug Falls. Fremont pictographs and petroglyphs line the creek. Gold-medal fishing water.

history: In 1869 John Wesley Powell's expedition lost a boat, much of its food and scientific instruments at Disaster Falls. Winnie's Rapid is supposedly named for Powell's daughter.

Buzz Holmstrom was the first to run the Green River in a rubber boat, and ran the whole river solo after being turned down as a boatman on the second Powell expedition. His 1937 inscription is on river left.
A dam was proposed at Echo Park in the 1950s and was never built, thanks to the efforts of Sierra Club director David Brower.
The 1869 Powell expedition named the Canyon of Lodore for Robert Southey’s poem “The Cataract of Lodore.” Sources credit Powell, or crew member Andrew Hall, with the name.
indigenous: Ute peoples have used this country for centuries, and the Fremont culture left rock art, granaries and campsites in the canyons about a thousand years ago. At Jones Hole you can find Fremont pictographs and petroglyphs. Look and photograph, but never touch the panels.
geology: At the Gates, the Green River cuts through red quartzite of the Uinta Mountain Group, rock roughly a billion years old and among the oldest in the monument. Downstream the walls change to Weber Sandstone and limestone, and the Mitten Park fault, with its folded and tilted layers, makes a dramatic display near Echo Park.
flows: The Green River in Lodore is controlled by Flaming Gorge Dam upstream, so the river runs year-round with the cold water of a tailwater. The Yampa River joins at Echo Park and adds muddy snowmelt in spring, speeding up the river below the confluence.

rules.d: In the high-use season camp only in your assigned sites, and pack up and clear the landing by noon so the next group can use it.
No camping on multiday trips at Echo Park, Rainbow Park or in Split Mountain Gorge.
One group per campsite, up to 25 people. Where sites are grouped, stay inside the posted boundaries.
The Superintendent may close campsites for bighorn lambing, bear activity or wildfire.
The printed, signed permit and the permit holder's ID, and the NPS boater's guide.
A fire pan with a 2.5-inch lip and at least 12 inches wide, with a fire blanket.
A river toilet system (groover or day-use kit).
One life jacket per person, plus one spare per 10 people. Spare oars or paddles: one per raft plus one per three small craft. Helmets for small craft.
Life jackets are required from Rainbow Park to the take-out.
Pets are not allowed on the river.

landmarks.name: Lodore boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Put-in, ranger station and campground (first come, first served). Steep canyon walls open to the Gates of Lodore.

landmarks.name: Zenobia Creek
landmarks.desc: River left. A rare Zenobia rock is here.

landmarks.name: Holmstrom inscription
landmarks.desc: River left. Left by Buzz Holmstrom and his companions Burg and Lundstrom on 9-11-37. Holmstrom was the first to run the Green River in a rubber boat.

landmarks.name: Yampa River confluence
landmarks.desc: The muddy Yampa joins the Green. In spring the river speeds up with the added water.

landmarks.name: Echo Park and Steamboat Rock
landmarks.desc: A wall almost a mile long that resembles a steamboat. The river makes a 180-degree turn around it. Echo Park campground is not for multiday river trips, and the tap may be dry.

landmarks.name: Mitten Park fault
landmarks.desc: A dramatic display of geology, running about a mile.

landmarks.name: Harpers Corner overlook
landmarks.desc: From the top of the canyon you can see both rivers.

landmarks.name: Echo Park dam site
landmarks.desc: The proposed 1955 dam site. Former Sierra Club director David Brower's efforts kept it from being built.

landmarks.name: Colorado-Utah state line
landmarks.desc: The Green River crosses from Colorado into Utah here.

landmarks.name: Sage Creek
landmarks.desc: River right. Listed in log order; mile is estimated.

landmarks.name: Red Wash Canyon
landmarks.desc: River right. Listed in log order; mile is estimated.

landmarks.name: Island Park
landmarks.desc: The river opens into a large valley meandering around islands, with views of the Uintah Mountains, Split Mountain and Ruple Ranch. This is Utah flat water: life jackets are not required for people over 14, except in inflatable kayaks.

landmarks.name: Rainbow Park boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Life jackets are required from here to the take-out. Not a camp for multiday trips.

landmarks.name: Split Mountain Gorge
landmarks.desc: The river cuts through in a short, rapid-filled run to the take-out. No camping in the gorge.

landmarks.name: Warm spring
landmarks.desc: A natural warm spring flows into the river, a good stop to warm up in cool early-season weather.

landmarks.name: Split Mountain boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Take-out. A working dinosaur quarry, museum and gift shop are just minutes away.

notes.camp: *Camps are assigned by site in the high-use season and must be vacated by noon. Camp high above the river: side canyons flash flood, and bighorn lambing or bear activity can close sites.
notes.hike: *Look at rock art, ruins and historic inscriptions but never touch or take anything. Hikes are hot and exposed; carry water and watch for rattlesnakes.

access.note: Emergency vehicle access only; not a trip put-in or take-out

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery May to September

items.d: High-use season applications are taken on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31. Results are emailed by mid-February. Pick the Gates of Lodore launch and Split Mountain take-out. About 300 permits are awarded each year for the Green and Yampa combined.
Each person may submit one high-use lottery application, and multiple applications forfeit any trip won. Applicants must be at least 18.
Low-use trips and unclaimed high-use dates open for reservation on March 6 at 8 a.m. Mountain Standard Time.
In the high-use season you camp only in sites assigned to your trip. Campsites are first come at the Gates of Lodore campground before launch.
Standard high-season Green River trips are 4 days. You may request one extra day for $35, refunded if denied. Requests are decided 30 days before launch.
The second Monday of May through the second Friday of September. The rest of the year is low-use. Flaming Gorge Dam regulates the flow, so the Green can usually be floated most of the year.
$185 per trip. Park entrance and campground fees are separate.
Permit fees are nonrefundable, except an overlength fee when the extra day is denied.
Up to 25 per site.
Split Mountain Campground can be reserved on Recreation.gov from mid-April to late September. Below Split Mountain, only small craft (canoes, duckies, kayaks) may take out at Placer Point.
River Runners Transport in Vernal, Utah has run shuttles. A 2018 report said it required a three-car minimum and may not shuttle a single private group in the low season. Confirm.
Private boaters need qualifying experience and equipment. Trips must be self-guided.
Reports range from about 600 cfs (rapids technical; Lucifer pinned a boat for three hours) to about 2,300 cfs from Flaming Gorge. Hell's Half Mile was run in an oar rig at 1,800 cfs.
